findings.claim: Secukinumab 10 mg/kg IV (days 1 and 22) did not improve CDAI vs placebo at week 6 in moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease; the change was numerically worse on drug, and the trial stopped early for futility.
findings.endpoint: Mean change in CDAI at 6 weeks
findings.studyContext: Phase 2 randomized double-blind, terminated for futility at interim analysis
findings.limitations: Small, short, single phase 2 trial; one dose regimen; the placebo response was large.

findings.claim: Published report concluded IL-17A blockade with secukinumab was ineffective in active Crohn's disease, with more adverse events (including infections, with fungal infections only on drug) than placebo.
findings.supportingPassage: Blockade of IL-17A was ineffective and higher rates of adverse events were noted compared with placebo.
findings.population: 59 patients with moderate to severe CD
findings.endpoint: Probability of CDAI reduction ≥50 points over placebo at week 6; safety
findings.studyContext: Same study as NCT00584740 (results publication), not independent corroboration
findings.limitations: Small proof-of-concept; Bayesian primary analysis with historical placebo; 8/39 drug vs 2/20 placebo stopped for insufficient effect.

findings.claim: Case series report new-onset or worsening IBD in patients treated with IL-17 inhibitors (including secukinumab) for psoriasis/spondyloarthritis, suggesting a possible protective role of IL-17A in the gut. Causality is not established.
findings.supportingPassage: IL-17A inhibitors are rarely associated with new or worsening inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)
findings.limitations: Case reports; no denominator or control; abstract excerpt only; different populations from Crohn's trial.

findings.claim: Open Targets gives a low overall IL17A–Crohn disease association (0.1), driven mainly by literature (0.503), with modest clinical (0.137) and RNA expression (0.126) evidence. This is a ranking, not a probability of success.
findings.supportingPassage: Overall association score 0.1 (datatypes: literature 0.503, clinical 0.137, rna_expression 0.126)

findings.claim: Secukinumab is an IL-17A inhibitor antibody with max phase 4 overall (approved for psoriasis, PsA, AS), but Crohn's disease max phase is 2. Phase reflects development stage, not efficacy in Crohn's.
An experimental 2.6 Å crystal structure of secukinumab Fv bound to human IL-17A is available (PDB 9SFX), so target engagement by this antibody is structurally characterized.

gaps.description: Did not retrieve the full results of the open-label extension NCT01009281 (n=7, terminated), or any later trial of IL-17A inhibition in Crohn's disease. Mechanistic data on IL-17A's gut-barrier role were also not retrieved.
